court: High Court of Judicature at Madras

parties.respondent_defendant: M.Swaminathan, Naresh, T.Inderkumar, T.Charulatha, and T.Girishi

facts_of_case: The Executor seeks revocation of the Probate granted in O.P.No.408 of 2014. The applicants claim to be the second wife and son born through the second wife of G.Ramakrishna, husband of the Testatrix Parvathi.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party claiming a marriage to prove it by leading evidence.
legal_principles.held: Relying upon the aforesaid documents, Mr.S.Parthasarathy, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the applicants would contend that the marriage has been proved and the 1st applicant being the son born through the said marriage would be an illegitimate son and would be entitled to succeed to the estate of his father in view of Section 16 of the Hindu Marriage Act.

legal_principles.principle: The law is clear that a discrepancy in the evidence does not necessarily mean that there was no marriage.
legal_principles.held: No doubt, true, that there is a discrepancy in the date of marriage in the evidence of PW1. PW1 has studied only upto VIII Standard and she has deposed in the year 2018 about the marriage that had taken place in the year 1973 i.e., nearly about 45 years after the event.

outcome.final_order: The Probate granted by this Hon'ble Court dated 25.02.2015 in O.P.No.408 of 2014 is revoked.

keywords: Latin Maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
